messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging oncall-mike: sudden KV cache memory growth and NCCL stall pattern detected in tp-shard-pool-7. Alerts: kv_cache_growth x10, continuous_batch_queue_length x6, nccl_op_timeouts x150. Affected nodes: gpu-41,gpu-42,gpu-43. Notable customer impact: transient 503 spike ~1.2% in eu-west-1 on /v1/chat.

mike: ACK. grabbing runtime logs and metrics dashboard. cs-erin, any customer reports yet?

cs-erin: getting pings from two enterprise customers, both reporting retries and increased latency. opening tickets and notifying account owners.

ananya: tailing pods now. seeing repeated "kv_shard_miss -> prefetch flood" logs: "kv_prefetch enqueue 1024 keys" from feeder threads. Also NCCL WARNs: "NCCL ERROR op 123 timeout" around the same timestamps.

joel: can we get pod resource states?

ananya: ```kubectl get pods -n redwood-runtime -l app=tp-shard-pool-7 -o wide
# gpu-41 tp-shard-7-0 Running MEM% 45
# gpu-42 tp-shard-7-1 Running MEM% 92
# gpu-43 tp-shard-7-2 Running MEM% 88
```

lisa: gpu-42 shows KV working set thrash. looks like one shard got the hot keys. uneven KV partitioning + aggressive prefetch = eviction storm.

ryan: was there a recent config or rollout?

mike: last runtime flag change 25m ago: continuous_batcher.prefetch_window increased from 32 -> 128 and prefetch_enabled=true enabled for larger parallelism. timeline matches.

joel: that explains it. the larger prefetch window multiplies per-request prefetched keys, and without a partition cap a single TP shard can be overwhelmed.

ananya: confirmed: logs show clients with multi-request bursts causing the same partition id to receive most keys. also see NCCL collectives stalling when memory pressure spikes.

mike: immediate mitigations: 1) toggle continuous_batcher.prefetch_enabled=false on tp-shard-pool-7, 2) set max_batch_tokens=256 for hostgroup, 3) evict local shard hotset by restarting tp-shard-7-1 (gpu-42), 4) temporarily enable per-shard memory alarms to auto-shed new partitions. Who can run these?

joel: I'll flip the prefetch flag and lower max_batch_tokens now. patching runtime config.

infra-bot: runtime-config update started by joel on tp-shard-pool-7.

ananya: restarted tp-shard-7-1 (gpu-42). pod came back healthy; memory dropped to ~38% after warmup. KV eviction rate for that pod returned to baseline. NCCL timeouts dropped significantly but a few lingering errors seen for in-flight ops.

sara: running synthetic smoke tests against /v1/chat in eu-west-1. p95 latency improved from 2.4s -> 1.1s. 5xxs back to normal.

cs-erin: notified affected customers with a brief: we had transient errors and latency, actions taken to stabilize, we'll follow up with full postmortem within 72h.

lisa: we still have uneven partition mapping in the routing table. proposing a short-term partition-stealing rebalancer: when a shard exceeds 40% of keys in a sliding window, reassign a small subset of keys round-robin to adjacent shards. I'll draft a conservative hotfix.

joel: agree. will run hotfix in canary pool tp-shard-pool-9 first. also adding a temporary circuit-breaker to the prefetch path to cap per-request prefetch keys to 256 regardless of the configured window.

incident-bot: update: severity = sev2 (partial service degradation, limited customers). paging paused.

mike: handoff notes for next oncall (ananya): current state: prefetch disabled on pool-7, max_batch_tokens set to 256, one pod restarted; metrics stable; canary for partition-stealing hotfix in staging. Monitor kv_evictions and nccl_op_timeouts; escalate if nccl timeouts > baseline*2.

ananya: taking oncall. will monitor dashboards and keep CS in loop.

joel: hotfix PR up: partition-stealing + prefetch circuit-breaker. running stress tests under synthetic skewed key distribution. so far no regressions; planning staged rollout.

infra-bot: canary rollout to tp-shard-pool-9: batch 1/3 success.

mike: cs-erin, please follow up with the two impacted customers with ETA for postmortem and mitigation summary. include mention of targeted hotfix and timeline.

cs-erin: sending notes now.

ananya: monitoring shows nccl_timeouts at 0 for last 20m, kv_evictions back to normal baseline, continuous_batch_queue length stable. marking incident mitigated.

lisa: follow-ups logged: 1) implement prefetch circuit-breaker with safe defaults, 2) ship partition-stealing rebalancer within 48h, 3) add metric that surfaces per-shard key concentration > 30%, 4) add an autoscaler to rebalance partitions if a shard memory > 80% for >2m. I'll own the postmortem.

mike: assigning postmortem owner = lisa. postmortem due in 72h. handoff complete to ananya. if anything spikes, re-page. :thumbsup:
